NASB.1: Now it came about when the king lived in his house, and the LORD had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,
NASB.2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, 'See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within tent curtains.'
NASB.3: Nathan said to the king, 'Go, do all that is in your mind, for the LORD is with you.'
NASB.4: But in the same night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
NASB.5: 'Go and say to My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD, 'Are you the one who should build Me a house to dwell in?
NASB.6: 'For I have not dwelt in a house since the day I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt, even to this day; but I have been moving about in a tent, even in a tabernacle.
NASB.7: 'Wherever I have gone with all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel, which I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, 'Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?'''
NASB.8: 'Now therefore, thus you shall say to My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts, 'I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over My people Israel.
NASB.9: 'I have been with you wherever you have gone and have cut off all your enemies from before you; and I will make you a great name, like the names of the great men who are on the earth.
NASB.10: 'I will also appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, that they may live in their own place and not be disturbed again, nor will the wicked afflict them any more as formerly,
NASB.11: even from the day that I commanded judges to be over My people Israel; and I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD also declares to you that the LORD will make a house for you.
NASB.12: 'When your days are complete and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come forth from you, and I will establish his kingdom.
NASB.13: 'He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
NASB.14: 'I will be a father to him and he will be a son to Me; when he commits iniquity, I will correct him with the rod of men and the strokes of the sons of men,
NASB.15: but My lovingkindness shall not depart from him, as I took [it] away from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
NASB.16: 'Your house and your kingdom shall endure before Me forever; your throne shall be established forever.'''
NASB.17: In accordance with all these words and all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
NASB.18: Then David the king went in and sat before the LORD, and he said, 'Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
NASB.19: 'And yet this was insignificant in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, for You have spoken also of the house of Your servant concerning the distant future. And this is the custom of man, O Lord GOD.
NASB.20: 'Again what more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD!
NASB.21: 'For the sake of Your word, and according to Your own heart, You have done all this greatness to let Your servant know.
NASB.22: 'For this reason You are great, O Lord GOD; for there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
NASB.23: 'And what one nation on the earth is like Your people Israel, whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people and to make a name for Himself, and to do a great thing for You and awesome things for Your land, before Your people whom You have redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, [from] nations and their gods?
NASB.24: 'For You have established for Yourself Your people Israel as Your own people forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
NASB.25: 'Now therefore, O LORD God, the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house, confirm [it] forever, and do as You have spoken,
NASB.26: that Your name may be magnified forever, by saying, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel'; and may the house of Your servant David be established before You.
NASB.27: 'For You, O LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, have made a revelation to Your servant, saying, 'I will build you a house'; therefore Your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to You.
NASB.28: 'Now, O Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are truth, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.
NASB.29: 'Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken; and with Your blessing may the house of Your servant be blessed forever.'

NKJV.1: Now it came to pass when the king was dwelling in his house, and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies all around,
NKJV.2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells inside tent curtains.”
NKJV.3: Then Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
NKJV.4: But it happened that night that the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
NKJV.5: “Go and tell My servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD: “Would you build a house for Me to dwell in?
NKJV.6: For I have not dwelt in a house since the time that I brought the children of Israel up from Egypt, even to this day, but have moved about in a tent and in a tabernacle.
NKJV.7: Wherever I have moved about with all the children of Israel, have I ever spoken a word to anyone from the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?’ ” ’
NKJV.8: Now therefore, thus shall you say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts: “I took you from the sheepfold, from following the sheep, to be ruler over My people, over Israel.
NKJV.9: And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you, and have made you a great name, like the name of the great men who are on the earth.
NKJV.10: Moreover I will appoint a place for My people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own and move no more; nor shall the sons of wickedness oppress them anymore, as previously,
NKJV.11: since the time that I commanded judges to be over My people Israel, and have caused you to rest from all your enemies. Also the LORD tells you that He will make you a house.
NKJV.12: “When your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who will come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
NKJV.13: He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
NKJV.14: I will be his Father, and he shall be My son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
NKJV.15: But My mercy shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
NKJV.16: And your house and your kingdom shall be established forever before you. Your throne shall be established forever.” ’ ”
NKJV.17: According to all these words and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
NKJV.18: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD; and he said: “Who am I, O Lord GOD? And what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
NKJV.19: And yet this was a small thing in Your sight, O Lord GOD; and You have also spoken of Your servant’s house for a great while to come. Is this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?
NKJV.20: Now what more can David say to You? For You, Lord GOD, know Your servant.
NKJV.21: For Your word’s sake, and according to Your own heart, You have done all these great things, to make Your servant know them.
NKJV.22: Therefore You are great, O Lord GOD. For there is none like You, nor is there any God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
NKJV.23: And who is like Your people, like Israel, the one nation on the earth whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people, to make for Himself a name—and to do for Yourself great and awesome deeds for Your land—before Your people whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, the nations, and their gods?
NKJV.24: For You have made Your people Israel Your very own people forever; and You, LORD, have become their God.
NKJV.25: “Now, O LORD God, the word which You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, establish it forever and do as You have said.
NKJV.26: So let Your name be magnified forever, saying, ‘The LORD of hosts is the God over Israel.’ And let the house of Your servant David be established before You.
NKJV.27: For You, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore Your servant has found it in his heart to pray this prayer to You.
NKJV.28: “And now, O Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.
NKJV.29: Now therefore, let it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue before You forever; for You, O Lord GOD, have spoken it, and with Your blessing let the house of Your servant be blessed forever.”

ESV.1: Now when the king lived in his house and the LORD had given him rest from all his surrounding enemies,
ESV.2: the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells in a tent.”
ESV.3: And Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
ESV.4: But that same night the word of the LORD came to Nathan,
ESV.5: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD: Would you build me a house to dwell in?
ESV.6: I have not lived in a house since the day I brought up the people of Israel from Egypt to this day, but I have been moving about in a tent for my dwelling.
ESV.7: In all places where I have moved with all the people of Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges  of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’
ESV.8: Now, therefore, thus you shall say to my servant David, ‘Thus says the LORD of hosts, I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, that you should be prince  over my people Israel.
ESV.9: And I have been with you wherever you went and have cut off all your enemies from before you. And I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones of the earth.
ESV.10: And I will appoint a place for my people Israel and will plant them, so that they may dwell in their own place and be disturbed no more. And violent men shall afflict them no more, as formerly,
ESV.11: from the time that I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. Moreover, the LORD declares to you that the LORD will make you a house.
ESV.12: When your days are fulfilled and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who shall come from your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
ESV.13: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
ESV.14: I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. When he commits iniquity, I will discipline him with the rod of men, with the stripes of the sons of men,
ESV.15: but my steadfast love will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away from before you.
ESV.16: And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me.  Your throne shall be established forever.’”
ESV.17: In accordance with all these words, and in accordance with all this vision, Nathan spoke to David.
ESV.18: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me thus far?
ESV.19: And yet this was a small thing in your eyes, O Lord GOD. You have spoken also of your servant's house for a great while to come, and this is instruction for mankind, O Lord GOD!
ESV.20: And what more can David say to you? For you know your servant, O Lord GOD!
ESV.21: Because of your promise, and according to your own heart, you have brought about all this greatness, to make your servant know it.
ESV.22: Therefore you are great, O LORD God. For there is none like you, and there is no God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
ESV.23: And who is like your people Israel, the one nation on earth whom God went to redeem to be his people, making himself a name and doing for them  great and awesome things by driving out before your people,  whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, a nation and its gods?
ESV.24: And you established for yourself your people Israel to be your people forever. And you, O LORD, became their God.
ESV.25: And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house, and do as you have spoken.
ESV.26: And your name will be magnified forever, saying, ‘The LORD of hosts is God over Israel,’ and the house of your servant David will be established before you.
ESV.27: For you, O LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, have made this revelation to your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to you.
ESV.28: And now, O Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are true, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
ESV.29: Now therefore may it please you to bless the house of your servant, so that it may continue forever before you. For you, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with your blessing shall the house of your servant be blessed forever.”

NLT.1: When King David was settled in his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all the surrounding enemies,
NLT.2: the king summoned Nathan the prophet. “Look,” David said, “I am living in a beautiful cedar palace, but the Ark of God is out there in a tent!”
NLT.3: Nathan replied to the king, “Go ahead and do whatever you have in mind, for the LORD is with you.”
NLT.4: But that same night the LORD said to Nathan,
NLT.5: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘This is what the LORD has declared: Are you the one to build a house for me to live in?
NLT.6: I have never lived in a house, from the day I brought the Israelites out of Egypt until this very day. I have always moved from one place to another with a tent and a Tabernacle as my dwelling.
NLT.7: Yet no matter where I have gone with the Israelites, I have never once complained to Israel’s tribal leaders, the shepherds of my people Israel. I have never asked them, “Why haven’t you built me a beautiful cedar house?”’
NLT.8: “Now go and say to my servant David, ‘This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies has declared: I took you from tending sheep in the pasture and selected you to be the leader of my people Israel.
NLT.9: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have destroyed all your enemies before your eyes. Now I will make your name as famous as anyone who has ever lived on the earth!
NLT.10: And I will provide a homeland for my people Israel, planting them in a secure place where they will never be disturbed. Evil nations won’t oppress them as they’ve done in the past,
NLT.11: starting from the time I appointed judges to rule my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. “‘Furthermore, the LORD declares that he will make a house for you — a dynasty of kings!
NLT.12: For when you die and are buried with your ancestors, I will raise up one of your descendants, your own offspring, and I will make his kingdom strong.
NLT.13: He is the one who will build a house — a temple — for my name. And I will secure his royal throne forever.
NLT.14: I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he sins, I will correct and discipline him with the rod, like any father would do.
NLT.15: But my favor will not be taken from him as I took it from Saul, whom I removed from your sight.
NLT.16: Your house and your kingdom will continue before me for all time, and your throne will be secure forever.’”
NLT.17: So Nathan went back to David and told him everything the LORD had said in this vision.
NLT.18: Then King David went in and sat before the LORD and prayed, “Who am I, O Sovereign LORD, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?
NLT.19: And now, Sovereign LORD, in addition to everything else, you speak of giving your servant a lasting dynasty! Do you deal with everyone this way, O Sovereign LORD?
NLT.20: “What more can I say to you? You know what your servant is really like, Sovereign LORD.
NLT.21: Because of your promise and according to your will, you have done all these great things and have made them known to your servant.
NLT.22: “How great you are, O Sovereign LORD! There is no one like you. We have never even heard of another God like you!
NLT.23: What other nation on earth is like your people Israel? What other nation, O God, have you redeemed from slavery to be your own people? You made a great name for yourself when you redeemed your people from Egypt. You performed awesome miracles and drove out the nations and gods that stood in their way.
NLT.24: You made Israel your very own people forever, and you, O LORD, became their God.

WEB.1: When the king lived in his house, and Yahweh had given him rest from all his enemies all around,

WEB.4: That same night, Yahweh’s word came to Nathan, saying,
WEB.5: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘Yahweh says, “Should you build me a house for me to dwell in?
WEB.6: For I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought the children of Israel up out of Egypt, even to this day, but have moved around in a tent and in a tabernacle.
WEB.7: In all places in which I have walked with all the children of Israel, did I say a word to any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’”’
WEB.8: Now therefore tell my servant David this, ‘Yahweh of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people, over Israel.
WEB.9: I have been with you wherever you went, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth.
WEB.10: I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not afflict them any more, as at the first,
WEB.11: and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I will cause you to rest from all your enemies. Moreover Yahweh tells you that Yahweh will make you a house.
WEB.12: When your days are fulfilled, and you sleep with your fathers, I will set up your offspring  after you, who will proceed out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom.
WEB.13: He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
WEB.14: I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men;
WEB.15: but my loving kindness will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before you.
WEB.16: Your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you. Your throne will be established forever.”’”
WEB.17: Nathan spoke to David all these words, and according to all this vision.
WEB.18: Then David the king went in, and sat before Yahweh; and he said, “Who am I, Lord  Yahweh, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
WEB.19: This was yet a small thing in your eyes, Lord Yahweh; but you have spoken also of your servant’s house for a great while to come; and this among men, Lord Yahweh!
WEB.20: What more can David say to you? For you know your servant, Lord Yahweh.
WEB.21: For your word’s sake, and according to your own heart, you have worked all this greatness, to make your servant know it.
WEB.22: Therefore you are great, Yahweh God. For there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
WEB.23: What one nation in the earth is like your people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem to himself for a people, and to make himself a name, and to do great things for you, and awesome things for your land, before your people, whom you redeemed to yourself out of Egypt, from the nations and their gods?
WEB.24: You established for yourself your people Israel to be your people forever; and you, Yahweh, became their God.
WEB.25: Now, Yahweh God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as you have spoken.
WEB.26: Let your name be magnified forever, saying, ‘Yahweh of Armies is God over Israel; and the house of your servant David will be established before you.’
WEB.27: For you, Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, have revealed to your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house.’ Therefore your servant has found in his heart to pray this prayer to you.
WEB.28: “Now, O Lord Yahweh, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
WEB.29: Now therefore let it please you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, Lord Yahweh, have spoken it. Let the house of your servant be blessed forever with your blessing.”

CSB17.1: When the king had settled into his palace <sup>ⓒ</sup> and the LORD had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,

CSB17.8: “So now this is what you are to say to my servant David: ‘This is what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the pasture, from tending the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.9: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have destroyed all your enemies before you. I will make a great name <sup>ⓘ</sup> for you like that of the greatest on the earth. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.10: I will designate a place <sup>ⓚ</sup> for my people Israel and plant them, <sup>ⓛ</sup> so that they may live there and not be disturbed again. Evildoers will not continue to oppress them as they have done
CSB17.11: ever since the day I ordered judges to be over my people Israel. <sup>ⓜ</sup> I will give you rest from all your enemies. “‘The LORD declares to you: The LORD himself will make a house for you.

CSB17.14: I will be his father, and he will be my son. <sup>ⓒ</sup> When he does wrong, I will discipline him with a rod of men and blows from mortals.

CSB17.18: Then King David went in, <sup>ⓗ</sup> sat in the LORD’s presence, and said, Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house that you have brought me this far?
CSB17.19: What you have done so far <sup>[2]</sup> was a little thing to you, Lord GOD, for you have also spoken about your servant’s house in the distant future. And this is a revelation <sup>[3]</sup> for mankind, Lord GOD.
CSB17.20: What more can David say to you? You know your servant, <sup>ⓘ</sup> Lord GOD.
CSB17.21: Because of your word and according to your will, you have revealed all these great things to your servant.
CSB17.22: This is why you are great, <sup>ⓙ</sup> Lord GOD. There is no one like you, and there is no God besides you, <sup>ⓚ</sup> as all we have heard confirms.
CSB17.23: And who is like your people Israel? God came to one nation on earth in order to redeem a people for himself, to make a name for himself, and to perform for them <sup>[4]</sup> great and awesome acts, <sup>[5]</sup> driving out nations and their gods before your people you redeemed for yourself from Egypt. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.24: You established your people Israel to be your own people forever, and you, LORD, have become their God. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.25: Now, LORD God, fulfill the promise forever that you have made to your servant and his house. Do as you have promised,
CSB17.26: so that your name will be exalted forever, when it is said, “The LORD of Armies is God over Israel.” The house of your servant David <sup>ⓝ</sup> will be established before you
CSB17.27: since you, LORD of Armies, God of Israel, have revealed this to your servant when you said, “I will build a house for you.” Therefore, your servant has found the courage to pray this prayer to you.
CSB17.28: Lord GOD, you are God; your words are true, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.

AMP.1: When King David lived in his house (palace) and the LORD had given him rest from all his surrounding enemies,
AMP.2: the king said to Nathan the prophet, "See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within tent curtains."
AMP.3: And Nathan said to the king, "Go, do everything that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you."
AMP.4: But it happened that night that the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,
AMP.5: "Go and tell My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD, "Should you be the one to build Me a house in which to dwell?
AMP.6: For I have not dwelt in a house since the day I brought the sons (descendants) of Israel up from Egypt, even to this day; but I have been moving about in a tent, even in a tabernacle.
AMP.7: Wherever I have gone with all the Israelites, did I speak a word to any from the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, asking, 'Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?'"'
AMP.8: So now, say this to My servant David, 'Thus says the LORD of hosts, "I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over My people Israel.
AMP.9: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you; and I will make you a great name, like that of the great men of the earth.
AMP.10: I will appoint a place for My people Israel and will plant them, so that they may live in a place of their own and not be disturbed again. The wicked will not afflict them again, as formerly,
AMP.11: even from the day that I appointed judges over My people Israel; and I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD also declares to you that He will make a house (royal dynasty) for you.
AMP.12: When your days are fulfilled and you lie down [in death] with your fathers (ancestors), I will raise up your descendant after you, who shall be born to you, and I will establish his kingdom.
AMP.13: He [is the one who] shall build a house for My Name and My Presence, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
AMP.14: I will be his Father, and he shall be My son. When he commits iniquity (wrongdoing), I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the strokes of the sons of man.
AMP.15: But My lovingkindness and mercy will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
AMP.16: Your house (royal dynasty) and your kingdom will endure forever before Me; your throne will be established forever."'"
AMP.17: Nathan spoke to David in accordance with all these words and all of this vision.
AMP.18: Then King David went in and sat [in prayer] before the LORD, and said, "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house (family), that You have brought me this far?
AMP.19: Yet this was very insignificant in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, for You have spoken also of Your servant's house (royal dynasty) in the distant future. And this is the law and custom of man, O Lord GOD.
AMP.20: What more can David say to You? For You know (acknowledge, choose) Your servant, O Lord GOD.
AMP.21: Because of Your word (promise), and in accordance with Your own heart, You have done all these great and astounding things to let Your servant know (understand).
AMP.22: Therefore You are great, O Lord GOD; for there is none like You, and there is no God besides You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
AMP.23: What one nation on earth is like Your people Israel, whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people and to make a name for Himself, and to do great and awesome things for Yourself and for Your land, before Your people whom You have redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, from nations and their gods?
AMP.24: You established for Yourself Your people Israel as Your people forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
AMP.25: Now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word [of the covenant] that You have spoken in regard to Your servant and his house (royal dynasty); and do just as You have spoken,
AMP.26: so that Your Name may be magnified forever, saying, 'The LORD of hosts (armies) is God over Israel;' and may the house (royal dynasty) of Your servant David be established before You.
AMP.27: For You, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant, saying, 'I will build you a house (royal dynasty).' For that reason Your servant has found courage to pray this prayer to You.
AMP.28: And now, O Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are truth, and You have promised this good thing to Your servant.

MSG.1: Before long, the king made himself at home and God gave him peace from all his enemies.

MSG.4: But that night, the word of God came to Nathan saying,

MSG.7: And in all my travels with Israel, did I ever say to any of the leaders I commanded to shepherd Israel, 'Why haven't you built me a house of cedar?'
MSG.8: "So here is what you are to tell my servant David: The God-of-the-Angel-Armies has this word for you: I took you from the pasture, tagging along after sheep, and made you prince over my people Israel.

MSG.10: And I'm going to set aside a place for my people Israel and plant them there so they'll have their own home and not be knocked around any more. Nor will evil men afflict you as they always have,
MSG.11:
even during the days I set judges over my people Israel. Finally, I'm going to give you peace from all your enemies.

MSG.14: I'll be a father to him, and he'll be a son to me. When he does wrong, I'll discipline him in the usual ways, the pitfalls and obstacles of this mortal life.

MSG.24: You established for yourself a people—your very own Israel!—your people permanently. And you, God, became their God.
MSG.25: "So now, great God, this word that you have spoken to me and my family, guarantee it permanently! Do exactly what you've promised!

MSG.28: "And now, Master God, being the God you are, speaking sure words as you do, and having just said this wonderful thing to me,

NET.9: I was with you wherever you went, and I defeated all your enemies before you. Now I will make you as famous as the great men of the earth.
NET.10: I will establish a place for my people Israel and settle them there; they will live there and not be disturbed any more. Violent men will not oppress them again, as they did in the beginning
NET.11: and during the time when I appointed judges to lead my people Israel. Instead, I will give you relief from all your enemies. The LORD declares to you that he himself will build a dynastic house for you.
NET.12: When the time comes for you to die, I will raise up your descendant, one of your own sons, to succeed you, and I will establish his kingdom.
NET.13: He will build a house for my name, and I will make his dynasty permanent.
NET.14: I will become his father and he will become my son. When he sins, I will correct him with the rod of men and with wounds inflicted by human beings.
NET.15: But my loyal love will not be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
NET.16: Your house and your kingdom will stand before me permanently; your dynasty will be permanent.’”
NET.17: Nathan told David all these words that were revealed to him.
NET.18: King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O LORD God, and what is my family, that you should have brought me to this point?
NET.19: And you didn’t stop there, O LORD God! You have also spoken about the future of your servant’s family. Is this your usual way of dealing with men, O LORD God?
NET.20: What more can David say to you? You have given your servant special recognition, O LORD God!
NET.21: For the sake of your promise and according to your purpose you have done this great thing in order to reveal it to your servant.
NET.22: Therefore you are great, O LORD God, for there is none like you! There is no God besides you! What we have heard is true!
NET.23: Who is like your people, Israel, a unique nation on the earth? Their God went to claim a nation for himself and to make a name for himself! You did great and awesome acts for your land, before your people whom you delivered for yourself from the Egyptian empire and its gods.
NET.24: You made Israel your very own people for all time. You, O LORD, became their God.
NET.25: So now, O LORD God, make this promise you have made about your servant and his family a permanent reality. Do as you promised,
NET.26: so you may gain lasting fame, as people say, ‘The LORD of hosts is God over Israel!’ The dynasty of your servant David will be established before you,
NET.27: for you, O LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, have told your servant, ‘I will build you a dynastic house.’ That is why your servant has had the courage to pray this prayer to you.
NET.28: Now, O sovereign LORD, you are the true God! May your words prove to be true! You have made this good promise to your servant!
NET.29: Now be willing to bless your servant’s dynasty so that it may stand permanently before you, for you, O sovereign LORD, have spoken. By your blessing may your servant’s dynasty be blessed on into the future!”
